insights.headline: Gold reclaims $4,180 on fading October Fed-hike bets as festive demand lifts Delhi gold to Rs 1.5 lakh
insights.summary: Remarks by Fed Chair Kevin Warsh cut the implied chance of an October rate hike to below one-in-six, lifting spot gold toward $4,190 and silver above $57.80. In India, Delhi gold climbed Rs 400 to Rs 1,50,300 per 10 grams on pre-Dussehra buying, with domestic metal at a premium for the first time in three months. About 17 mutual fund houses have paused fresh inflows into gold ETF fund-of-funds following a SEBI nudge, though existing SIPs continue. A firm rupee capped spot gains even as MCX futures advanced.
points: Spot gold near $4,185; silver above $57.80 as October Fed-hike odds fall below one-in-six after Warsh's Bangkok remarks.
Delhi gold up Rs 400 to Rs 1,50,300/10g on festive demand; silver steady at Rs 2.15 lakh/kg; bullion markets shut Tuesday for Dussehra.
17 AMCs halt fresh subscriptions in gold ETF FoFs from Oct 15-16; existing SIPs and redemptions unaffected.
Rupee's seventh straight rise trimmed spot gold to Rs 1,46,406/10g even as MCX futures gained on global cues.
Hindustan Zinc's Q2 profit more than doubled on higher metal prices; silver output and revenue rose.

trending.title: October hike odds collapse after Warsh remarks
trending.summary: Traders now see the Fed holding at the Oct 27-28 meeting after Warsh refused to pre-judge policy; spot gold reclaimed $4,185 and silver topped $57.80, while December hike bets linger on hot PPI data.

trending.title: Festive demand returns with a premium
trending.summary: Delhi gold crossed Rs 1.5 lakh per 10g on Dussehra-eve buying, and domestic metal traded at a premium last week for the first time in three months; analysts expect demand to build toward Diwali.

trending.title: The gold-fund door shuts for new money
trending.summary: About 17 fund houses paused fresh inflows into gold ETF fund-of-funds after a reported SEBI nudge; existing SIPs run on, while RBI fixed the Oct 19 SGB Series VII redemption at Rs 14,614.

trending.title: Silver's two tracks
trending.summary: Silver gained on the softer Fed outlook but kept stalling below $58; Hindustan Zinc's Q2 silver revenue rose even as spot prices eased.

trending.title: Central banks keep buying the dips
trending.summary: Goldman Sachs estimates central banks bought about 79 tonnes in August, and gold fund holdings just hit a 2026 record even as prices corrected.

items.title: Gold edges higher as traders ease rate-hike bets on Warsh speech
items.summary: Spot gold climbed toward $4,190 after Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's remarks were read as favoring a pause at the Oct 27-28 meeting, with traders cutting the implied chance of an October hike to below one-in-six. A hot inflation print last week had lifted hike bets and the dollar; Warsh's comments halted the dollar's gains. Silver rose about 1.5% to $57.80.

items.title: Gold climbs Rs 400 to Rs 1.5 lakh per 10 gm as festive buying elevates demand
items.summary: Delhi gold rose Rs 400 to Rs 1,50,300 per 10 grams, inclusive of taxes, on Monday as festive demand picked up ahead of Dussehra; silver held steady at Rs 2.15 lakh per kg. HDFC Securities' Saumil Gandhi said domestic gold traded at a premium last week for the first time in three months and expects retail demand to build toward Diwali. Bullion markets shut Tuesday for Dussehra.

items.title: Did Mutual Funds Stop Gold Investments? What Investors Need to Know
items.summary: About 17 fund houses, including ICICI Prudential, HDFC, Tata, Invesco, SBI and Kotak, have paused fresh subscriptions in their gold ETF fund-of-funds from Oct 15-16 - covering lump sums, switch-ins and new SIP/STP registrations. Existing SIP instalments continue and redemptions stay open. Reuters reported the curbs followed a nudge from SEBI; the notices gave no reason.

items.title: Spot gold slightly down on firm rupee; markets see no Fed rate hike in Oct
items.summary: Spot gold in India's major markets slipped Rs 20 to Rs 1,46,406 per 10 grams as the rupee rose for a seventh straight session, cheapening dollar-denominated metal. But December MCX futures added 0.2% to Rs 1,48,221 and COMEX futures held near $4,197.80 as traders priced in a Fed hold in October after Warsh's remarks, with softer crude adding support.

items.title: Gold, silver prices today: What could drive bullion rates this week
items.summary: COMEX gold rose 0.30% to $4,193.60 and silver 0.51% to $57.60 on Monday, with gold touching $4,208.40 intraday, as safe-haven demand and lower Treasury yields offset inflation worries and Hormuz risk. The piece recaps last week's domestic correction - MCX gold fell 2.4% to about Rs 1.47 lakh, silver 6.4% to about Rs 2.11 lakh - and quotes IBJA's Prithviraj Kothari on short-covering.

items.title: Gold slips, silver gains as oil retreats and Fed-pause expectations hold - Kitco AM Report
items.summary: Kitco's morning note has spot gold slightly lower at $4,159.70 (-0.11%) and spot silver higher at $57.30 (+0.77%) in early US trading, as retreating oil prices and lower Treasury yields supported metals while sticky inflation and expectations of further Fed tightening capped buying. A later afternoon note put spot near $4,150, little changed as investors awaited the Oct 27-28 Fed meeting.

items.title: Hindustan Zinc Q2 profit more than doubles on higher metal prices; silver output up 20%
items.summary: Hindustan Zinc's consolidated net profit more than doubled to Rs 6,412 crore in Q2 FY27 as higher metal prices and record output lifted revenue 76.5% to Rs 15,093 crore, margin widening to 42%. Silver production rose 20% to 173 tonnes and silver sales revenue more than doubled, driving about 45% of profitability; Jefferies said firmer silver prices improved the profit outlook.

items.title: Gold prices slid, but gold fund holdings just hit a record. Here's who keeps buying
items.summary: Investors poured $10B into gold-backed ETFs worldwide in September, lifting holdings 67 tonnes to a record 4,256 tonnes, World Gold Council data show; the $31B July-September haul was a record quarter. Central banks added 39 tonnes in August (170 tonnes year-to-date), with China buying for a 22nd straight month - patient buyers treating lower prices as an opportunity.

items.title: Gold and silver head for volatile week amid crude oil spike, West Asia worries
items.summary: PTI reports MCX December gold fell Rs 3,581 (-2.4%) last week to Rs 1.47 lakh/10g, and silver Rs 14,568 (-6.4%) to Rs 2.11 lakh/kg. The rupee's jump to 94.8 from ~96.8 in five sessions on RBI intervention cut import costs, dragging domestic prices down ~5x the global fall. Analysts expect a capped, choppy week: Brent near $110, West Asia tensions, and Tuesday's Dussehra morning closure.

items.title: Central Banks Are Buying Gold - So Why Is the Yellow Metal Still Under Pressure?
items.summary: Fawad Razaqzada argues gold's bearish trend remains intact: elevated oil, 10-year Treasury yields above 5.05% and sticky inflation keep tightening bets alive, capping rallies. He flags $4,100 as the line to watch - a break could expose $4,000 - with resistance at $4,223-$4,260. Until that pressure eases, recoveries face an uphill struggle and the burden of proof is on the bulls.

items.title: IBJA's Surendra Mehta sees gold rallying 10-12% to $4,700 by November 30
items.summary: IBJA national secretary Surendra Mehta told ET Now Swadesh he expects gold to rally 10-12% by November 30, potentially reaching $4,700 an ounce, as bond yields ease below 5.1% and crude stabilises near $105. He put the downside at 4-5% (a move toward $3,850 not ruled out) and said India's festive season could support prices, barring fresh geopolitical escalation.

items.title: RBI sets SGB 2020-21 Series VII redemption at Rs 14,614 for October 19
items.summary: The RBI has fixed October 19, 2026 as the premature redemption date for Sovereign Gold Bond 2020-21 Series VII at Rs 14,614 per gram, based on IBJA's average closing prices of October 14-16. Online subscribers gain 192.22% and offline buyers 189.33% in capital gains, alongside 2.5% annual interest; holders must route requests through their receiving offices within the notification window.

items.title: Gold on Dhanteras: celebrate the ritual, rethink the investment
items.summary: A Mint column argues Dhanteras gold buying is a cherished tradition that should not be mistaken for investing: most purchases are jewellery with making charges that vanish on resale, or coins sitting in rented lockers. Buying an asset on a set date because it is auspicious is consumption, not a financial plan - enjoy the ritual, but judge the purchase on its merits.

items.title: Iran warns of 'new operational plan' as vessel attacks spread across the Gulf
items.summary: Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei said Tehran has prepared a 'new operational plan' if the US resumes attacks, after UKMTO reported a tug hit by two projectiles near Khor Fakkan on Sunday and a tanker struck off Saudi Arabia on Saturday. The weekend strikes extend a campaign that has kept Hormuz shipping below pre-war levels, underpinning gold's safe-haven bid as West Asia tensions run high.

items.title: Silver stalls below $58.00 despite US dollar weakness
items.summary: XAG/USD kept a moderately bullish tone but bulls failed to find acceptance near the $58.00 area, with the US dollar index edging down less than 0.1% on Monday. Markets priced only a 12% chance of an October Fed hike, down from nearly 60% a month ago, after Chair Warsh declined forward guidance; elevated energy prices kept inflation well above target.
